headline: Adds the term deposits module supporting opening, maturing, and breaking 3, 6, or 12-month fixed-rate deposits.
summary: Introduces the Deposits module with domain entities, application service, API controller, database table, and DI registration. Customers can lock at least 500 in whole cents for 3, 6, or 12 months at fixed rates or break early without interest. Staff can mature deposits once due, transferring principal and rounded simple interest via the ledger.
business: Customers can lock funds of at least 500 for 3, 6, or 12 months at 2.0%, 2.5%, or 3.0% annual interest, or break early to recover principal only. Staff trigger payouts after maturity.

reasons.text: Controller-level Customer policy prevents Staff from calling mature endpoint
reasons.claim: DepositsController is annotated with [Authorize(Policy = Policies.Customer)] at the class level, which ASP.NET Core applies conjunctively with the action-level [Authorize(Policy = Policies.Staff)] on the Mature endpoint. Consequently, Staff users who do not have the Customer role receive a 403 Forbidden response when attempting to mature deposits.
reasons.suggested_fix: Remove [Authorize(Policy = Policies.Customer)] from the DepositsController class declaration. The Open and Break endpoints already declare [Authorize(Policy = Policies.Customer)] on their respective actions.
reasons.say: Staff without customer credentials cannot trigger term deposit payouts after maturity, leaving customers waiting for their money. Ask the author to move the customer restriction off the DepositsController class onto customer-only actions.
reasons.say_facts: Consequently, Staff users who do not have the Customer role receive a 403 Forbidden response when attempting to mature deposits. Ask for a fix before merging.

reasons.text: Controller-level Customer policy blocks Staff access to Mature endpoint
reasons.claim: In ASP.NET Core, [Authorize] attributes are evaluated additively across class and action levels. Because DepositsController is decorated with [Authorize(Policy = Policies.Customer)], the Mature action decorated with [Authorize(Policy = Policies.Staff)] requires callers to satisfy both policies, returning HTTP 403 Forbidden to staff accounts and preventing staff execution.
reasons.suggested_fix: Remove [Authorize(Policy = Policies.Customer)] from the class declaration (or replace it with [Authorize] without policy), as Open, Mature, and Break already specify their respective Customer and Staff policies on each action method.
reasons.say: Staff cannot mature deposits and pay out customer funds because DepositsController stacks customer and staff permissions together. Ask the author to separate the policies per endpoint so staff-only access works.
reasons.say_facts: Because DepositsController is decorated with [Authorize(Policy = Policies.Customer)], the Mature action decorated with [Authorize(Policy = Policies.Staff)] requires callers to satisfy both policies, returning HTTP 403 Forbidden to staff accounts and preventing staff execution. Ask for a fix before merging.

reasons.detail: Customers can lock funds of at least 500 for 3, 6, or 12 months at 2.0%, 2.5%, or 3.0% annual interest, or break early to recover principal only. Staff trigger payouts after maturity.
reasons.say: This change handles customer funds of 500 or more, fixed interest payouts, and early breaks. Verify the interest math, principal handling, and maturity payout rules against bank policy before signing off.
reasons.say_facts: This change has a high impact on customers or money: Customers can lock funds of at least 500 for 3, 6, or 12 months at 2.0%, 2.5%, or 3.0% annual interest, or break early to recover principal only. Staff trigger payouts after maturity. Confirm the business owner agrees.

reasons.text: Controller-level Customer authorization policy blocks Staff from mature endpoint
reasons.claim: In ASP.NET Core, authorization attributes combine additively. Because `[Authorize(Policy = Policies.Customer)]` is declared on DepositsController, the `Mature` action requires both `Policies.Customer` and `Policies.Staff`, which prevents pure Staff users from maturing deposits.
reasons.suggested_fix: Remove `[Authorize(Policy = Policies.Customer)]` from the controller class level (or replace with bare `[Authorize]`), keeping explicit policy checks on individual actions (`Open` and `Break` already specify `Policies.Customer`).
reasons.say: Because DepositsController combines customer and staff access rules, staff cannot mature deposits for customers. Check the endpoint permissions and ask for the customer-level restriction to be moved to individual endpoints.
reasons.say_facts: Because `[Authorize(Policy = Policies.Customer)]` is declared on DepositsController, the `Mature` action requires both `Policies.Customer` and `Policies.Staff`, which prevents pure Staff users from maturing deposits. Decide whether it must be fixed now.

reasons.text: Unbounded memory growth in DepositLocks ConcurrentDictionary
reasons.claim: DepositLocks stores a SemaphoreSlim for each deposit ID processed in MatureAsync and BreakAsync but never removes entries. Over the lifetime of the application, this static collection will grow unbounded as term deposits are matured or broken.
reasons.suggested_fix: Clean up unused semaphores using TryRemove once the lock is released and no other threads are waiting, or use a size-bounded eviction cache.
reasons.evidence: private static readonly ConcurrentDictionary<Guid, SemaphoreSlim> DepositLocks = new();
reasons.say: Locking entries in DepositLocks are never cleaned up, which can slowly exhaust server memory and disrupt deposit services. Ask the author to add cleanup or a bounded cache for these locks.
reasons.say_facts: Over the lifetime of the application, this static collection will grow unbounded as term deposits are matured or broken. Decide whether it must be fixed now.

reasons.text: Unbounded memory accumulation in static DepositLocks dictionary
reasons.claim: DepositLocks stores a SemaphoreSlim instance for every deposit ID passed to MatureAsync or BreakAsync without an eviction or cleanup mechanism. Because entries are added before confirming whether the deposit exists and are never pruned, this results in continuous memory growth over time and creates a potential resource exhaustion vector.
reasons.suggested_fix: Use keyed lock striping or a size-bounded/sliding cache with eviction, or rely on database-level row locking / concurrency tokens rather than an unbounded static dictionary.
reasons.evidence: private static readonly ConcurrentDictionary<Guid, SemaphoreSlim> DepositLocks = new();
reasons.say: Uncleaned lock entries in DepositLocks pile up even for invalid deposit requests, risking server slowdown or downtime for customers. Ask the author to remove finished locks or bound the collection.
reasons.say_facts: Because entries are added before confirming whether the deposit exists and are never pruned, this results in continuous memory growth over time and creates a potential resource exhaustion vector. Decide whether it must be fixed now.

reasons.text: Static DepositLocks dictionary leaks memory over time
reasons.claim: DepositService allocates a SemaphoreSlim for each deposit ID into a static ConcurrentDictionary that is never pruned. Every deposit that is matured or broken leaves an entry in memory indefinitely, causing unbounded resource consumption over the application's lifetime.
reasons.suggested_fix: Rely on database transaction concurrency control (such as concurrency tokens or row versioning) rather than an unbounded in-memory static dictionary, or evict lock entries once transitions complete.
reasons.evidence: private static readonly ConcurrentDictionary<Guid, SemaphoreSlim> DepositLocks = new();
reasons.say: DepositLocks keeps a lock in memory forever for every matured or broken deposit, risking outages over time. Ask how locks will be evicted once deposit processing finishes.
reasons.say_facts: Every deposit that is matured or broken leaves an entry in memory indefinitely, causing unbounded resource consumption over the application's lifetime. Decide whether it must be fixed now.

reasons.text: DepositsController endpoints and authorization policies have zero test coverage
reasons.claim: DepositsController defines endpoints with class-level Policies.Customer and action-level Policies.Staff, but has zero test references across the test suite. The combination of class-level Customer policy with action-level Staff policy on Mature risks rejecting Staff callers unless explicitly verified by tests.
reasons.suggested_fix: Add controller tests covering Open, Mature, and Break endpoints and verify the correct policies and status codes.
reasons.evidence:
[Authorize(Policy = Policies.Customer)]
public sealed class DepositsController : ControllerBase
reasons.say: DepositsController endpoints and access rules have no automated tests, leaving staff payouts and customer protections unverified. Ask for endpoint tests covering both allowed and forbidden user roles.
reasons.say_facts: The combination of class-level Customer policy with action-level Staff policy on Mature risks rejecting Staff callers unless explicitly verified by tests. Decide whether it must be fixed now.

reasons.text: No test coverage for non-EUR multi-currency deposit lifecycle
reasons.claim: All test fixtures hardcode EUR accounts and verify ledger balances only in EUR. The requirement highlights multi-currency ledger routing to DepositHolding and InterestExpense as an operational risk, but non-EUR flows are unexercised.
reasons.suggested_fix: Add a test scenario creating and maturing a deposit with a non-EUR account (such as USD) to verify multi-currency holding and expense account routing.
reasons.say: Multi-currency deposits are untested, so interest payouts and holding accounts in non-EUR currencies could route money incorrectly. Ask for tests covering non-EUR deposits from opening through maturity and early break.
reasons.say_facts: The requirement highlights multi-currency ledger routing to DepositHolding and InterestExpense as an operational risk, but non-EUR flows are unexercised. Decide whether it must be fixed now.

reasons.text: Staff-only maturity enforcement required by acceptance criteria is not tested
reasons.claim: The acceptance criteria mandate automated xUnit tests verifying Staff-only maturity enforcement. Existing tests only invoke IDepositService.MatureAsync directly using a caller that still has the Customer role, without asserting that non-Staff callers are rejected.
reasons.suggested_fix: Add an integration or controller test verifying that POST api/deposits/{id}/mature permits Staff callers and returns Forbid or Unauthorized for Customer callers.
reasons.say: There is no automated proof that only staff can trigger deposit payouts, risking unauthorized payouts or blocked operations. Ask for tests verifying that non-staff callers are rejected on maturity.
reasons.say_facts: The acceptance criteria mandate automated xUnit tests verifying Staff-only maturity enforcement. Decide whether it must be fixed now.
